steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Obsession, is it?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This is your obsession.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What's wrong with a little obsession?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I don't care if it's irrational, meaningless, or futile - when I make up my mind to do something, I do it!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why do you think we fight?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Those empty platitudes of yours - did you think they weren't a form of obsession too?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why are each of us here, if not for our own obsessions?
A shot rings out.
However, the target was not Andoain.
Before he realizes it, his gun had left his hand.
But he feels at ease.
For his gun will forever remain in Laterano.
He may never say it, but how can anyone help but love Laterano?
Those peaceful days, those joyful times, those happy moments.
But because of this 'love', he has had regrets, guilt, shame, and doubts.
He may never become a true Lateran.
But in this moment, when he thinks about his gun staying here forever...
At this very moment, under the glare of the faces looking at him...
A kind of peace floats to the surface like a bubble, then pops.
He walked ten thousand miles on the path of faith and doubt.
From one path to the next.
He thought he was wandering the wilderness, far from his roots.
But perhaps this was not true.
In more ways than one.
He whispered a word of gratitude.
No one will ever hear it, not in the past, present, or future.
But it was enough.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Finally. I thought maybe you had dozed off.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Come on, cut me some slack. It's hard finding a good sniping vantage point.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: This is it, Andoain. Hands up—

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: (Whispers) Here... out of obsession...

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Watch out!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: How does he still have enough strength left for Arts?!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: How could one find salvation alone?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, not salvation, but a life with dignity.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: You come before me because of your sense of justice, and I arrived here because of mine.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It comes to myth, to obsession, to the ultimately futile crossing... the path was always beneath my feet.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Why do we place our hopes on salvation? What we have done is not for the sake of salvation.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But to save ourselves.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Have you come to your senses, Andoain? Then look me in the eye—I felt like I was shooting a target dummy.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'll walk my own path, whether this is my mission or not.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I must thank you, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're welcome. I'll be sure to tell your friends about this epiphany at your funeral.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: As for right now, you're—
I'm afraid it's not yet time for that. I still have a use for him.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Someone blew up one of the support beams. We need to go!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Who the—?!

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The explosion was approved. I personally submitted the application and stamped it myself.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Oren! Why you—!

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What are you doing, Oren? Is this what you came to do?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Welp, cat's out of the bag.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: (Go, Andoain. I'll find you later.)

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Fiammetta, Mostima... perhaps we'll meet again.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Wheresoever that may be, let us hold onto our obsessions.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: For as you say, they are why we exist.

steps.name: Hotel Manager
steps.text: Please, miss, I must ask you to come down from the signboard.

steps.name: Hotel Manager
steps.text: I'll have to call the Guards if you don't comply.

steps.name: Hotel Manager
steps.text: But while we're at it, I just have to know.

steps.name: Hotel Manager
steps.text: How on Terra did you get up there with a wheelchair?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Where there's a will, there's a way.

steps.name: Hotel Manager
steps.text: That dust cloud... another explosion? There's been too many of those lately. It's starting to seem more like a fireworks show than a conference.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Um, excuse me? Could you give me a hand?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Sometimes it's easier to get up than to get down.

steps.name: Angry Ambassador
steps.text: You must be joking! What is wrong with Laterano's crisis management? That explosion damaged my collection! I demand an explanation!

steps.name: Impatient Ambassador
steps.text: The Lateran bells are ringing for the first time in a thousand years? Was this prepared by His Holiness as a special welcome for us?

steps.name: Hesitant Ambassador
steps.text: Being with you barbarians is too much to bear. If not for my respect for His Holiness, I'd—

steps.name: Elegant Ambassador
steps.text: Tell the cook to prepare dinner. I refuse to attend another Lateran banquet.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Can these people really bring change? Most of them are opportunists, at best.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Yes. This is something that only Laterano can do - Laterano, the city of miracles, forever fair and just.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Your Holiness... I will pray for us.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Rare to see you so nervous, Velliv.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: I'm too old for parlor tricks. All I can do is to keep walking, as far as I can.

steps.name: Friar
steps.text: Your Holiness, the broadcast is ready.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: The Pope
steps.text: Let my words and deeds honor my name and title.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Greetings, honored guests. I am Yvangelista XI, and I welcome you on behalf of Laterano.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We are facing a great challenge, one that threatens not just Laterano, but all nations across Terra.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: As you know, our countries are built on the backs of nomadic cities.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Indeed, the advent of such cities established the very concept of the modern nation state.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: In the past, a state was simply a gathering of people of similar lifestyles, huddled together for safety in the face of Catastrophe. 'National borders' were simply whatever lay within their sights.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: This all changed with the birth of nomadic cities.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: As is the human condition, conflict began to arise as these states interacted with each other.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Perhaps even the word 'conflict' is an understatement.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I saw the fall of Gaul with my own eyes.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The 'Capital of the World' fell overnight. Armored battleships went silent, and the Old Vanguard of Gaul was reduced to ash.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But it was more than Gaul that fell that night. It was the fall of civilization itself.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: All the might of the Gaulish Emperor and his legions could not save an empire that once stood proudly as the center of all lands.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What, then, could possibly preserve our own civilization, that the people of Terra have painstakingly built, piece by piece, under the dark cloud of Catastrophe?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Laterano gave much for the war that engulfed the entire continent. Our Messengers crossed both the wilderness and the royal courts, building Laterano's reputation.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Sankta heard your calls for peace.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But our lands had seen too many shades of this so-called peace, pooling in the dark corners of castles, palaces, and tents.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We've seen the birth of secrets, meant only to benefit a select few, that lie in wait to undermine peace and order when least expected.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The old wars of conquest may be a distant memory, but in their place we have tacit understandings and secret dealings, that determine the fates of lives and nations from out of sight.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Today though, Revelation has come.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It is my hope that the process of building peace be transparent from the very start. That we will all reject secret agreements between the few.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: There are questions that anyone who does not cling to the past, anyone who is concerned about the future of this land, should be asking.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: How do we ensure the survival of civilization?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: How many people are endangered when peace is threatened?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: What does safety for one country mean for the safety of other countries?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Civilization is key to survival. Peace is something to be shared with others, not hoarded for oneself.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: As such, I call for the establishment of an accord of mutual assurance between nations.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: We have far more common interests than many would imagine.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Terra must stand together, or fall together.

a.text: Yvangelista XI's speech on March 18th, 1099, later known as the 'Lateran Declaration,' is quoted on the first page of every edition of the International Summit Handbook.
